input.quote: Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.
input.rationale: Searches for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "accelerate", and all termination provisions (§§ 8–10, 27.3) return no amount payable by Customer as liquidated damages, a penalty, an early-termination fee, or a minimum charge on termination. The only "penalty" reference (§ 27.3) confirms Customer may terminate without penalty; § 7.3 bars interest on amounts ultimately found not due; and § 24.4 bars fee acceleration on Customer change of control. This meets the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties), so no redline is warranted. The take-or-pay minimum commitment in § 2.1 is the closest economic analogue but is a purchase commitment rather than a liquidated-damages or penalty mechanic and is addressed under the minimum-commitment rule; we do not flag it twice here. Noted for context only: the body contains no service-credit regime, which is referenced to the service-level exhibit under § 2.2.
